newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan money rates dip after cut in repo rates.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan money rates dip after cut in repo rates.

text.p: Pakistan's money market rates dipped on Wednesday after the State (central) Bank of Pakistan trimmed its repo rate to 19 percent from 20 percent, dealers said.

"The inter-bank money market opened amid uncertainty after the State Bank cut its repo rate by one percent," a dealer said. "Some nominal overnight deals were done at around 19 percent, but by midday the borrowers managed to bring the rates down to 12 percent and 14 percent."
The rates bounced back to 17 percent towards the close, but most deals were struck at 18 percent, dealers said.
"In line with our expectations, the State Bank further reduced its cut-off in today's open market operation and it picked a nominal amount at 15.90 percent," one dealer said.
